newsitem.title: USA: P&G/Tambrands may face antitrust hurdle-arbs.
newsitem.headline: P&G/Tambrands may face antitrust hurdle-arbs.

text.p: Wall Street arbitrageurs hailed Procter & Gamble Co's $50-per-share bid for Tambrands Inc, but said it may face antitrust scrutiny if regulators review the new company on the basis of the overall feminine-hygiene market, instead of by individual product.

Because Tambrands' tampons including the Tampax brand dominate the market while Procter & Gamble is a powerhouse in sanitary napkins, the $1.85 billion deal may run into regulatory oppositon if the Federal Trade Commission adopts a broad market examination, the arbs said.
"If the FTC looks at this as a feminine protection market, they (the companies) have a problem," said an arbitrageur.

"And these are products with a high profile that lots of people use. The fact that McDonnell Douglas Corp and Boeing Co will merge to form the one manufacturer of commercial aircraft in the country does not seem to bother them (the FTC) maybe as much as if the price of tampon goes up $0.12," added the arb, who declined to be identified.

If the FTC adopts a broad scope to gauge the market concentration of a combined P&G/Tambrands, it would be the opposite tack taken by the commission in its fight against the $4 billion Office Depot Inc /Staples Inc merger, the arbs said.

In the Staples case, they said, the FTC is in effect arguing that the office-supply superstore retailers are a separate industry. The companies are arguing that their business is one distribution channel in the larger office-supply industry.

Because other U.S. feminine-hygiene companies hold sizable tampon market share unlike P&G, including Kimberly-Clark Corp with Kotex, Johnson & Johnson with o.b. and Playtex Products Inc, interest from them was unlikely because of potential antitrust issues.
A second arbitrageur who participated in this morning's conference call on the merger, which was closed to reporters, said, "The analysts like the deal. They think it makes a lot of sense."
In afternoon New York Stock Exchange trade, Tambrands shares were up 2-1/8 to 48-1/4, backing off an earlier session-high of 48-5/8, while P&G shares climbed 3-1/8 to 119.
Johnson & Johnson stock was unchanged at 54-5/8, Playtex slid 7/8 to 9-3/4 and Kimberly-Clark slipped 1/2 to 49-1/4.
